akero.heading: AKERO
akero.quality: This is now rarely grown, but is of interest only from its remarkable coloration.
akero.note: Book's synonyms Akera, Okera; 'Origin, probably Swedish'. Says nothing about taste.

alfriston.heading: ALFRISTON
alfriston.flavour: Flesh, crisp, pale yellow, sub-acid. This apple cooks a tender, golden brown with a delicious pear-like flavour.
alfriston.note: Synonyms Shepherd's Pippin, Shepherd's Seedling as in our aka; raised by Mr. Shepherd at Alfriston, Sussex. The pear-like flavour is of the cooked apple.

ard-cairn-russet.heading: ARD CAIRN RUSSET
ard-cairn-russet.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, good russet flavour.
ard-cairn-russet.note: An old Irish variety introduced by Hartland of Ard Cairn, Co. Cork.

baumanns-reinette.heading: BAUMANN'S REINETTE
baumanns-reinette.flavour: Flesh, white, crisp, juicy, slightly aromatic.
baumanns-reinette.quality: A remarkable cropper but of poor quality.
baumanns-reinette.storage: Culinary or dessert, December to January
baumanns-reinette.note: Synonyms Couronne des Dames, Reinette de Bolwyller as in our aka; raised probably by Van Mons.

baxters-pearmain.heading: BAXTER'S PEARMAIN
baxters-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, tender, pleasantly acid. It is rather too acid for some palates.
baxters-pearmain.storage: Dessert or culinary, December to February
baxters-pearmain.note: A Norfolk variety introduced by G. Lindley in 1821.

bietigheimer.heading: BIETIGHEIMER
bietigheimer.flavour: Flesh, firm, greenish-white, sweet but with no aroma.
bietigheimer.note: Bunyard treats Bietigheimer as a synonym of Rother Stettiner (Rouge de Stettin, 'more than twenty-five' synonyms) and says that is the correct name; the large crimson culinary fruit fits our record, but the Stettiner confusion makes the identity uncertain. His 'sweet' sits awkwardly with our sharp tag.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFER
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, pale yellow, poor flavour.
edelborsdorfer.quality: A worthless fruit in this country, except in very warm seasons.
edelborsdorfer.climate: A worthless fruit in this country, except in very warm seasons.
edelborsdorfer.note: Book gives G. Edelborsdorfer; German, recorded by Cordus in 1561; imported for Queen Charlotte.

fenouillet-gris.heading: CARAWAY RUSSET
fenouillet-gris.quality: A reliable sort still grown in old orchards.
fenouillet-gris.note: Bunyard: 'The correct name is Fenouillet Gris'; Leroy takes it for the Epice d'Hiver of Olivier de Serres. No mention of aniseed in the flesh description despite the name.

cellini.heading: CELLINI
cellini.flavour: Flesh, tender white, sub-acid, with curious balsamic flavour. Regular cropping is its chief recommendation, but the curious flavour appeals to some.
cellini.quality: Regular cropping is its chief recommendation
cellini.note: Synonym Phillips' Seedling; raised by Leonard Phillips, Vauxhall, about 1828. 'Balsamic' is not in our tag list.

dutch-mignonne.heading: DUTCH MIGNONNE
dutch-mignonne.quality: A most useful, fertile fruit. Considered by many to be worthy of dessert use late in the season.
dutch-mignonne.note: F. Reinette de Caux; G. Grosser Casseler Reinette; Paternoster - all in our aka. Bunyard: 'Grosser Casseler Reinette is the original name'.

frogmore-prolific.heading: FROGMORE PROLIFIC
frogmore-prolific.note: Raised in the Royal Gardens at Frogmore by Mr. Ingram.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh, tender, white, sub-acid. It cooks a brown colour, but is very sweet and rich.
gloria-mundi.quality: Too uncertain a cropper in most parts.
gloria-mundi.note: Synonyms Monstrous Pippin, Ox Apple, Mammoth as in our aka; first recorded in America in 1804.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellow, very sweet and rich.
golden-harvey.quality: One of the good old sorts which have been neglected.
golden-harvey.note: Synonyms Brandy Apple, Round Russet Harvey as in our aka; English, known early in the seventeenth century.

histon-favourite.heading: HISTON FAVOURITE
histon-favourite.flavour: Flesh, soft, pale yellow, juicy, slight aromatic flavour.
histon-favourite.quality: A nice fruit, but rather too small with me.
histon-favourite.storage: Dessert or cooking, November to December
histon-favourite.note: Book's synonym Oliver's Seedling; raised at Histon by John Chivers (our aka Chivers' Seedling).

kandil-sinap.heading: KANDIL SINAP
kandil-sinap.flavour: Flesh, white, crisp, tender, juicy, and slight flavour.
kandil-sinap.quality: It is one of the most popular market varieties in the Crimea.
kandil-sinap.note: F. Candile Sinope; 'This Russian fruit is remarkable for its elongated barrel shape'.

manningtons-pearmain.heading: MANNINGTON'S PEARMAIN
manningtons-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellow, fair flavour. The flavour of this variety is only fair
manningtons-pearmain.quality: as there are so many better at this season I consider it not worth growing.

melon.heading: MELON
melon.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, tender, juicy, somewhat aromatic.
melon.quality: A good useful late fruit now seldom met with.
melon.note: The New York Melon (Norton's Melon) from the Heman Chapin orchard, East Bloomfield, introduced by Ellwanger & Barry in 1845 - same apple as ours despite the homonym risk.

nanny.heading: NANNY
nanny.flavour: Flesh, tender, greenish yellow, a little sweet, but of no remarkable flavour.
nanny.note: A Sussex apple. Bunyard has a separate SEPTEMBER BEAUTY (line 5293, Laxton c.1885), so our aka September Beauty is probably a different apple.

ontario.heading: ONTARIO
ontario.flavour: Flesh, crisp, juicy, pale yellow, sub-acid.
ontario.quality: An excellent late variety, worthy of extended cultivation.
ontario.storage: It does not shrivel when kept long.
ontario.note: Wagener x Northern Spy by Charles Arnold, Ontario, before 1874.

potts-seedling.heading: POTTS' SEEDLING
potts-seedling.quality: A useful kitchen fruit. Most valuable for small gardens.
potts-seedling.note: Synonyms Dean's Codlin, Holland Pippin (the latter is NOT our holland-pippin). Raised at Ashton-under-Lyne, dates from 1849.

reinette-du-canada.heading: REINETTE DU CANADA
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, of rich flavour.
reinette-du-canada.climate: Excellent in warm seasons. Very subject to canker.
reinette-du-canada.note: G. Pariser Rambour Reinette; 'some forty-eight synonyms'; known in France before 1771.

reinette-rouge-etoilee.heading: REINETTE ROUGE ETOILEE
reinette-rouge-etoilee.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, pale yellow with suffused red below skin, sub-acid, of slight strawberry flavour.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.quality: Of fair quality and most attractive in appearance.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.note: Synonyms Early Red Calville, Reinette Etoilee as in our aka; 'the Early Red Calville of Hogg'.

renown.heading: RENOWN
renown.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, firm, of pleasant flavour.
renown.storage: Dessert or culinary, October to November
renown.note: Raised by Charles Ross from the same cross as Charles Ross; Gard. Chron. 1908.

star-of-devon.heading: STAR OF DEVON
star-of-devon.flavour: Flesh, soft, nearly white, of poor flavour.
star-of-devon.quality: Up to the present no particular merit has been discovered.
star-of-devon.note: Raised by J. Garland, Broad Clyst, Devon; introduced 1905 by George Pyne, Topsham.

upton-pyne.heading: UPTON PYNE
upton-pyne.flavour: Flesh, firm, white, juicy, of brisk pine flavour.
upton-pyne.quality: Of very distinct flavour and likely to become popular.
upton-pyne.note: Raised by Mr. Pyne of Topsham, introduced in 1910.

venus-pippin.heading: VENUS PIPPIN
venus-pippin.flavour: Flesh, tender, pale yellow, juicy and refreshing flavour.
venus-pippin.quality: Rather too soft for market use and hardly worth retention.
venus-pippin.storage: Dessert or culinary, September to October
venus-pippin.note: Synonym Plumderity as in our aka; 'said to have been raised about 1800'.

wagener.heading: WAGENER
wagener.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, yellow, pleasantly flavoured.
wagener.quality: One of the best late varieties
wagener.note: G. Wageners Preis Apfel; raised in the garden of Abraham Wagener about 1796 at Dover, New York.

williams-favourite.heading: WILLIAM'S FAVOURITE
williams-favourite.quality: One of the best early dessert apples and well worthy of culture.
williams-favourite.note: Origin at Roxbury, U.S.A., about 1750. 'sott' is the OCR's misreading of 'soft' (left as printed so the quote validates).
